1.explanation:
1. cli/cli-flags.js defines and parses the --no-emulatedUserAgent flag but never wires it through correctly into the final settings (so even with that flag the system still thinks it should emulate a UA).

2. core/lib/emulation.js’s parseUseragentIntoMetadata() unconditionally injects Moto G4 metadata whenever formFactor==='mobile'. Because the code only looks at formFactor to pick device details, disabling screenEmulation or UA spoofing alone does not prevent it from labeling the run as “Moto G4.”

3. core/config/config-helpers.js’s resolveSettings() logic merges the default mobile UA back in after applying CLI flags, so flags.emulatedUserAgent=false is overwritten. The settings object seen by the report generator still has emulatedUserAgent===true and formFactor==='mobile', causing the report template to render the “Emulated Moto G4” string.

Fixing the bug requires:
- Ensuring --no-emulatedUserAgent actually sets settings.emulatedUserAgent to false in the merged settings (cli-flags.js + config-helpers.js).
- Adjusting parseUseragentIntoMetadata() or the report-generation template to skip Moto G4 metadata when settings.emulatedUserAgent===false (core/lib/emulation.js).
- (Optionally) augment resolveSettings() to preserve the real device flag and pass it through to the UI renderer so the footer can say "Testing on a real device..." instead of defaulting to "Emulated".
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse CLI against a real Android device (a Moto Power G) with screen emulation disabled, no UA spoofing (using --no-emulatedUserAgent), and DevTools–based throttling, the generated HTML footer still reads “Emulated Moto G4 with Lighthouse 9.6.8” (and shows the Moto G4 icon) instead of indicating that the audit was performed on a physical device.
